subproblems.title: Smooth approximation of a map that is Lipschitz near a set: McShane extension, mollification with local derivative bounds, and tangential vanishing of pulled-back forms (supplied Part 1, 5.5, 6.8)
subproblems.statement: Let m, m′ ∈ ℕ, G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} (ℝ^p = Eucl p), Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, A ⊆ ℝ^m and δ > 0, and assume G is Λ-Lipschitz on the open δ-neighbourhood thickening δ A. Then there are Ĝ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, maps G_j : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} (j ∈ ℕ) and L ∈ ℝ≥0 such that: (a) Ĝ is L-Lipschitz on ℝ^m and Ĝ = G on thickening δ A; (b) every G_j is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)) and L-Lipschitz on ℝ^m; (c) G_j → Ĝ uniformly on ℝ^m; (d) ‖fderiv ℝ G_j x‖ ≤ Λ for all j and all x ∈ thickening (δ/2) A; (e) (tangential vanishing) for all k ∈ ℕ, α ∈ SimonMultiIndex k m′, z ∈ ℝ^{m′}, ω ∈ TestFormOn univ k (on ℝ^{m′}) and ε > 0 such that every x ∈ thickening ε A with G(x) ∈ thickening ε (tsupport ω) satisfies G(x)_i = z_i for every i ∉ range α, and ω(y)(e_{α(1)}, …, e_{α(k)}) = 0 for every y ∈ ℝ^{m′} (e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1), there is r > 0 such that for all sufficiently large j and all x ∈ thickening r A the covector ω(G_j(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G_j x) is zero.

Source: Part 1 (1.1 McShane extension, 1.2 mollification with (a) smoothness, (b) locality and inherited constant coordinates, (c) local and global Lipschitz bounds) of the supplied proof of deformation_pushforward_homotopy, together with the mollifier argument of its 5.5 (local bound ‖DG_σ‖ ≤ Λ near the support, used for clause (1)) and of its 6.8 (the analytic core of Step 7: a mollified map whose normal coordinates are locally constant kills forms without tangential component). Here it is packaged for an arbitrary set A on whose δ-neighbourhood G is Lipschitz; the parent applies it with A = spt X.

Notation. ℝ^p = Eucl p with standard basis e_1, …, e_p (indexed by Fin p, e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1) and Euclidean norm |·|. For B ⊆ ℝ^p and ρ > 0, B_ρ := thickening ρ B = {x : infDist x B < ρ} (open; x ∈ B_ρ iff |x − b| < ρ for some b ∈ B; B ⊆ B_ρ). B_ρ(x) := ball x ρ. For a k-covector γ (continuous alternating k-linear map) and a linear map T, γ∘T denotes γ.compContinuousLinearMap T. A_δ := thickening δ A.

1. (McShane extension.) For i ∈ Fin m′ the coordinate G_i(x) := G(x)_i satisfies |G_i(x) − G_i(y)| ≤ |G(x) − G(y)| ≤ Λ|x − y| on A_δ, so G_i is Λ-Lipschitz on A_δ. By LipschitzOnWith.extend_real there is a Λ-Lipschitz Ĝ_i : ℝ^m → ℝ with Ĝ_i = G_i on A_δ. Put Ĝ(x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m′) ℝ).symm (fun i => Ĝ_i(x)), i.e. Ĝ(x)_i = Ĝ_i(x). Then Ĝ = G on A_δ, and |Ĝ(x) − Ĝ(y)|² = Σ_i |Ĝ_i(x) − Ĝ_i(y)|² ≤ m′Λ²|x − y|². Let L := √m′·Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 (NNReal.sqrt m′ * Λ); Ĝ is L-Lipschitz. This gives the first two conjuncts (LipschitzWith L Ĝ, EqOn Ĝ G (thickening δ A)).

2. (Mollifier.) Fix a C^∞ function ϕ : ℝ^m → ℝ with ϕ ≥ 0, ϕ(w) = 0 for |w| ≥ 1/2, compact support and ∫ϕ = 1 (take a smooth bump b ≥ 0, b(0) = 1, tsupport b ⊆ closedBall(0, 1/4), from exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset / ContDiffBump, and divide by ∫b > 0; the accepted declaration slicing_mb_sa_mollifier_exists of another branch states exactly this and may be reused by a later decomposition). For σ > 0 put ϕ_σ(w) := σ^{−m}ϕ(w/σ): C^∞, ≥ 0, ϕ_σ(w) = 0 for |w| ≥ σ/2, compact support, ∫ϕ_σ = 1 (substitution w = σu, Measure.integral_comp_smul). For a continuous H : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} put H_σ(x) := ∫ ϕ_σ(w)·H(x − w) dw (Bochner integral in ℝ^{m′}; the integrand is continuous with compact support in w, hence integrable). Facts:
 (a) H_σ is C^∞: H_σ is the convolution of ϕ_σ with H for the bilinear map lsmul (scalar times vector); ϕ_σ is C^∞ with compact support and H is continuous, hence locally integrable, so HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left gives ContDiff ℝ ∞ H_σ (the order ∞ = ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) of the statement).
 (b) (Locality.) The integrand vanishes for |w| ≥ σ/2, so H_σ(x) only involves H on B_σ(x). If H(y)_i = c for all y ∈ B_σ(x), then H_σ(x)_i = ∫ϕ_σ(w)H(x − w)_i dw = c∫ϕ_σ = c (the coordinate functional is continuous linear and commutes with the Bochner integral).
 (c) (Local Lipschitz bounds.) Suppose H is Λ′-Lipschitz on B_{2σ}(x). For y, y′ ∈ B_σ(x) and |w| < σ we have y − w, y′ − w ∈ B_{2σ}(x), so |H_σ(y) − H_σ(y′)| ≤ ∫ϕ_σ(w)|H(y − w) − H(y′ − w)| dw ≤ Λ′|y − y′|: H_σ is Λ′-Lipschitz on the open ball B_σ(x) ∋ x. Since H_σ is differentiable at x and Λ′-Lipschitz on a neighbourhood of x, ‖DH_σ(x)‖ ≤ Λ′ (for a unit vector v, |DH_σ(x)v| = lim_{h→0}|H_σ(x + hv) − H_σ(x)|/|h| ≤ Λ′; Mathlib norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn with the neighbourhood B_σ(x)). Also |H_σ(x) − H(x)| = |∫ϕ_σ(w)(H(x − w) − H(x))dw| ≤ ∫ϕ_σ(w)Λ′|w|dw ≤ Λ′σ (∫ϕ_σ = 1; x − w, x ∈ B_{2σ}(x)).
 (d) (Global bounds.) If H is L-Lipschitz on ℝ^m, then by the same computations H_σ is L-Lipschitz on ℝ^m and |H_σ(x) − H(x)| ≤ Lσ for every x.

3. (The sequence.) Let σ_j := δ/(8(j+1)) for j ∈ ℕ (so 0 < σ_j ≤ δ/8 and σ_j → 0) and G_j := Ĝ_{σ_j}.
 (i) Each G_j is C^∞ by 2(a), and L-Lipschitz by 2(d) applied to the L-Lipschitz Ĝ (fourth conjunct).
 (ii) sup_x |G_j(x) − Ĝ(x)| ≤ Lσ_j → 0 by 2(d), i.e. TendstoUniformly G_j Ĝ atTop (fifth conjunct).
 (iii) Let x ∈ A_{δ/2}. If |y − x| < 2σ_j ≤ δ/4 then infDist y A < δ/2 + δ/4 < δ, so B_{2σ_j}(x) ⊆ A_δ, where Ĝ = G is Λ-Lipschitz. By 2(c), ‖DG_j(x)‖ ≤ Λ (sixth conjunct).

4. (Tangential property, the last conjunct.) Let k, α : SimonMultiIndex k m′ (strictly increasing α : Fin k → Fin m′), z ∈ ℝ^{m′}, ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) and ε > 0 satisfy: (H1) every x ∈ A_ε with G(x) ∈ (tsupport ω)_ε has G(x)_i = z_i for all i ∉ range α; (H2) ω(y)(e_{α(1)}, …, e_{α(k)}) = 0 for every y. Put r₀ := min(ε, δ)/2 > 0 and r := r₀/2 > 0. Since σ_j → 0 there is j₀ with σ_j < min(r₀/4, ε/(4Λ + 4)) for all j ≥ j₀. Fix j ≥ j₀ and x ∈ A_r; write σ := σ_j, F := Ĝ, so G_j = F_σ. We show β := ω(F_σ(x))∘DF_σ(x) = 0.
 (4a) If F_σ(x) ∉ tsupport ω, then ω(F_σ(x)) = 0 (a point outside the topological support is outside the support), so β = 0.
 (4b) Assume F_σ(x) ∈ tsupport ω. Let y ∈ B_{2σ}(x). Then infDist y A < r + 2σ < r₀/2 + r₀/2 = r₀ ≤ min(ε, δ)/2, so y ∈ A_ε ∩ A_δ and F(y) = G(y). The ball B_{2σ}(x) lies in A_δ, where F = G is Λ-Lipschitz, so 2(c) gives |F_σ(x) − G(x)| ≤ Λσ, and hence |G(y) − F_σ(x)| ≤ |G(y) − G(x)| + |G(x) − F_σ(x)| ≤ 2Λσ + Λσ < ε. Thus G(y) lies within ε of the point F_σ(x) ∈ tsupport ω, i.e. G(y) ∈ (tsupport ω)_ε, and y ∈ A_ε; by (H1), F(y)_i = G(y)_i = z_i for all i ∉ range α.
 (4c) For x′ ∈ B_σ(x) we have B_σ(x′) ⊆ B_{2σ}(x), so by (4b) and 2(b), F_σ(x′)_i = z_i for every i ∉ range α. Hence for i ∉ range α the coordinate function x′ ↦ F_σ(x′)_i is constant on the open ball B_σ(x) ∋ x, its derivative at x vanishes, and (DF_σ(x)v)_i = 0 for every v ∈ ℝ^m. So DF_σ(x) maps ℝ^m into V_α := span{e_{α(1)}, …, e_{α(k)}}.
 (4d) (Alternating algebra.) Let γ := ω(F_σ(x)), an alternating k-linear form on ℝ^{m′} with γ(e_{α(1)}, …, e_{α(k)}) = 0 by (H2). Let u_1, …, u_k ∈ V_α and write u_p = Σ_q c_{pq} e_{α(q)}. By multilinearity γ(u_1, …, u_k) = Σ_{τ : Fin k → Fin k} (Π_p c_{p,τ(p)}) γ(e_{α(τ(1))}, …, e_{α(τ(k))}). If τ is not injective, two arguments coincide (α is injective) and the term vanishes because γ is alternating; if τ is a permutation, γ(e_{α∘τ}) = sign(τ)·γ(e_α) = 0. Hence γ(u) = 0 (equivalently γ(u) = det(c)·γ(e_α)). Applying this with u_p := DF_σ(x)v_p ∈ V_α (4c) gives β(v_1, …, v_k) = γ(DF_σ(x)v_1, …, DF_σ(x)v_k) = 0 for all v, so β = 0. (For k = 0, (H2) says γ = ω(F_σ(x)) = 0 directly.)
 Thus for every j ≥ j₀ and every x ∈ thickening r A the covector ω(G_j x).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ (G_j) x) vanishes; with r > 0 this is the required ∃ r, 0 < r ∧ ∀ᶠ j in atTop, …. ∎
proof_key_steps: McShane: extend each coordinate of G|A_δ by LipschitzOnWith.extend_real; the vector extension Ĝ is √m′Λ-Lipschitz and equals G on A_δ.

Mollifier ϕ_σ (C^∞, ≥ 0, support in B_{σ/2}(0), ∫ = 1); H_σ := ϕ_σ ⋆ H is C^∞, depends only on H|B_σ(x), inherits constant coordinates, is Λ′-Lipschitz on B_σ(x) (so ‖DH_σ(x)‖ ≤ Λ′) when H is Λ′-Lipschitz on B_{2σ}(x), and |H_σ − H| ≤ Λ′σ.
G_j := Ĝ_{σ_j}, σ_j = δ/(8(j+1)): smooth, L-Lipschitz, uniformly close to Ĝ, and ‖DG_j‖ ≤ Λ on A_{δ/2} because B_{2σ_j}(x) ⊆ A_δ.

Tangential vanishing: for σ_j < min(r₀/4, ε/(4Λ+4)), r₀ = min(ε,δ)/2, and x ∈ A_{r₀/2} with G_j(x) ∈ tsupport ω, every y ∈ B_{2σ_j}(x) has G(y) ∈ (tsupport ω)_ε, so the normal coordinates of G are z on B_{2σ_j}(x) and those of G_j are constant on B_{σ_j}(x).
Hence DG_j(x) maps into V_α = span{e_{α(i)}}, and an alternating k-form vanishing on e_α vanishes on V_α^k (β(u) = det(c)β(e_α)), so ω(G_j x)∘DG_j(x) = 0.

Source: Part 3, items 3.1–3.4 of the supplied proof of deformation_pushforward_homotopy (Simon Ch. 6, 2.17–2.22: slice forms, the product current [[0,1]]×X(φ) := ∫_0^1 X(φ^{(t)})dt, its mass and support, and the boundary formula ∂([[0,1]]×X) = {1}×X − {0}×X − [[0,1]]×∂X from (dψ)^{(t)} = ∂_tψ_t − d(ψ^{(t)})), together with the normality estimate M(∂Z) ≤ 2M(X) + M(∂X) of its Part 4. The coordinates are those of the frozen statement of iwl_cr_interval_product_im: the time coordinate is the 0-th coordinate.

Notation. ℝ^p = Eucl p, e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. For s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^m: cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι(v) := cons(0, v) (a linear isometry, ι(e_i) = e_{i.succ}); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 = cons(1, 0); j_s(x) := cons(s, x) = s·e₀ + ι(x) (affine, derivative ι, |j_s(x) − j_s(x′)| = |x − x′|). For y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}: t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)), so y = cons(t(y), tl(y)), t(cons(s,x)) = s, tl(cons(s,x)) = x, and |y|² = t(y)² + |tl(y)|². cyl(A) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1], tl(y) ∈ A}. For a q-covector γ, |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} γ(e_{I_1},…,e_{I_q})²)^{1/2}; ‖ω‖ := sup_y |ω(y)| for a form ω (finite for continuous compactly supported ω). D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q. M := mass, spt := support.
 Slice notions. For η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), a family φ : ℝ → D^k(ℝ^m) is a dt-slice family of η on [0,1] if φ_s(x)(v) = η(cons(s,x))(e₀, ιv_1, …, ιv_k) for s ∈ [0,1], x, v (exactly the hypothesis of the characterization ProdChar(X, Z): "Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ_s) ds for every η and every dt-slice family φ of η on [0,1]"). For ψ ∈ D^q(ℝ^{m+1}) and s ∈ ℝ, the horizontal slice ψ_s is the q-form ψ_s(x)(v) := ψ(cons(s,x))(ιv_1, …, ιv_q) (= j_s^#ψ).
 Reused facts: (R1) mass_bound (cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le): 0 ≤ B, M_W(T) ≤ ofReal B, tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ C for all x ⇒ |T(ω)| ≤ B·C; with W = univ and B = M(T).toReal: |T(ω)| ≤ M(T).toReal·C whenever M(T) < ∞. (R2) vanish_off_support (isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support): tsupport ω ∩ spt T = ∅ ⇒ T(ω) = 0. (R3) compatible_form (iwl_sp_exists_compatible_testForm). (R4) slice_forms (iwl_cr_ci_slice_testForm): every η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) has a dt-slice family φ^η defined for all s ∈ ℝ, with (s, x) ↦ φ^η_s(x) continuous.

1. (Coefficient bounds.) (C1) For a (k+1)-covector γ on ℝ^{m+1} let γ′(v) := γ(e₀, ιv_1, …, ιv_k). For strictly increasing I : Fin k → Fin m, γ′(e_I) = γ(e_0, e_{I_1.succ}, …, e_{I_k.succ}) is the coefficient of γ at the strictly increasing tuple Fin.cons 0 (succ ∘ I); this assignment is injective, so Σ_I γ′(e_I)² ≤ Σ_J γ(e_J)², i.e. |γ′| ≤ |γ|. (C2) Likewise for a q-covector γ on ℝ^{m+1}, γ″(v) := γ(ιv_1, …, ιv_q) satisfies |γ″| ≤ |γ| (I ↦ succ ∘ I is injective into strictly increasing tuples). Both γ ↦ γ′, γ ↦ γ″ are linear, so |γ′ − δ′| ≤ |γ − δ| and |γ″ − δ″| ≤ |γ − δ|. (C3) For any q-covector γ on ℝ^p, |γ| ≤ √(p^q)·‖γ‖ (operator norm): each coefficient satisfies |γ(e_I)| ≤ ‖γ‖Π|e_{I_i}| = ‖γ‖ and there are at most p^q tuples.

2. (Horizontal slices are test forms.) Let ψ ∈ D^q(ℝ^{m+1}) and s ∈ ℝ. The map j_s is C^∞ and proper (j_s⁻¹(K) is closed and bounded for compact K, since j_s is an isometric embedding). Apply (R3) with U = V = univ, A = univ, f = j_s: it yields η ∈ D^q(ℝ^m) with η(x) = ψ(j_s(x)).compContinuousLinearMap(Dj_s(x)) for all x (N ⊇ univ); since j_s(x) = s·e₀ + ι(x) is affine, fderiv ℝ j_s x = ι, so η = ψ_s. Also tsupport ψ_s ⊆ tl(tsupport ψ) =: K(ψ), a compact set independent of s; similarly tsupport φ^η_s ⊆ K(η) for every s.

3. (Continuity in s.) Let M(X) < ∞, η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and φ a dt-slice family of η on [0,1]. For s, s′ ∈ [0,1] and every x, by (C1) |φ_s(x) − φ_{s′}(x)| ≤ |η(cons(s,x)) − η(cons(s′,x))|. As η is continuous with compact support it is uniformly continuous, and |cons(s,x) − cons(s′,x)| = |s − s′|; with (C3) the right side tends to 0 uniformly in x as s′ → s. By (R1), |X(φ_s) − X(φ_{s′})| = |X(φ_s − φ_{s′})| ≤ M(X).toReal·sup_x|φ_s(x) − φ_{s′}(x)| → 0. Hence s ↦ X(φ_s) is continuous on [0,1]; this is conjunct (e) of part (I). Moreover |X(φ_s)| ≤ M(X).toReal·‖η‖ for s ∈ [0,1] by (C1) and (R1). The same argument applies to horizontal slices (with (C2)). In particular it applies to the family s ↦ ∂_sψ_s of step 7, which consists of the horizontal slices of the test form ψ′ = Dψ(·)(e₀).

4. (Current criterion.) (F5) If ω_j → 0 in the sense TestFormOnConverges (all supports in one compact K, iteratedFDeriv ℝ q ω_j → 0 uniformly on K for every q), then ‖ω_j‖ → 0: for q = 0, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ = ‖ω_j x‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), ω_j = 0 off K, and |ω_j(x)| ≤ √(p^k)‖ω_j(x)‖ by (C3). (F6) Hence if T₀ : D^q(ℝ^p) → ℝ is linear and |T₀(ω)| ≤ B‖ω‖ for all ω (some B ≥ 0), then T₀ is sequentially continuous at 0 and defines T ∈ D_q(ℝ^p) with T(ω) = T₀(ω); and for every ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ q univ (|ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x), T(ω) ≤ B, so M(T) ≤ ofReal B.

5. (Definition; conjuncts (a), (b), (c) of part (I).) Let M(X) < ∞ and B := M(X).toReal. For η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) let φ^η be given by (R4) and put Z₀(η) := ∫_0^1 X(φ^η_s) ds. If φ is any dt-slice family of η on [0,1], then φ_s = φ^η_s (as test forms, Subtype.ext and funext) for s ∈ [0,1], so ∫_0^1 X(φ_s) ds = Z₀(η) (intervalIntegral.integral_congr on uIcc 0 1 = [0,1]). Linearity: aφ^η + bφ^{η′} is a dt-slice family of aη + bη′, and both integrands are continuous on [0,1] (step 3), hence interval integrable, so Z₀(aη + bη′) = ∫_0^1 (aX(φ^η_s) + bX(φ^{η′}_s)) ds = aZ₀(η) + bZ₀(η′). Bound: |Z₀(η)| ≤ B‖η‖ (step 3 and intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const, interval of length 1). By step 4 there is Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with Z(η) = Z₀(η) for all η, and M(Z) ≤ ofReal(B) = M(X) (M(X) < ∞): conjunct (c). Conjunct (a), ProdChar(X, Z), is the first sentence of this step. Conjunct (b): if Z′ also satisfies ProdChar(X, Z′), then Z′(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ^η_s) ds = Z(η) for every η (φ^η is a dt-slice family on [0,1]), so Z′ = Z by GeometricCurrentOn.ext.

6. (Support; conjunct (d).) cyl(spt X) is closed (t, tl continuous; [0,1] and spt X closed). Let y₀ ∉ cyl(spt X); choose ρ > 0 with closedBall(y₀, 2ρ) ∩ cyl(spt X) = ∅ and put W := ball(y₀, ρ) (open, closure compact). Let η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with tsupport η ⊆ W. For s ∈ [0,1], tsupport φ^η_s ⊆ {x : cons(s,x) ∈ tsupport η} (support of φ^η_s lies in the preimage of support η under the continuous j_s, and the preimage of the closed set tsupport η is closed); if x ∈ spt X then cons(s,x) ∈ cyl(spt X), which is disjoint from tsupport η ⊆ W. So tsupport φ^η_s ∩ spt X = ∅, X(φ^η_s) = 0 by (R2), and Z(η) = 0. Thus Z vanishes on W, W lies in the zero region of Z, and y₀ ∉ spt Z. Hence spt Z ⊆ cyl(spt X).

7. (Calculus identity.) Let ψ ∈ D^q(ℝ^{m+1}) (q = k for the boundary formulas below) and y = cons(s, x). By exteriorDerivative_apply (extDeriv_apply), dψ(y)(u_0, …, u_q) = Σ_{i=0}^{q} (−1)^i Dψ(y)(u_i)(u_0, …, û_i, …, u_q) (i.e. Fin.removeNth). Take u_0 = e₀, u_i = ιv_i (1 ≤ i ≤ q):
 dψ(cons(s,x))(e₀, ιv_1, …, ιv_q) = Dψ(cons(s,x))(e₀)(ιv_1, …, ιv_q) − Σ_{i=1}^{q} (−1)^{i−1} Dψ(cons(s,x))(ιv_i)(e₀, ιv_1, …, ι̂v_i, …, ιv_q).
 The first term is ∂_sψ_s(x)(v), where ∂_sψ_s denotes the horizontal slice at s of the q-form ψ′(y) := Dψ(y)(e₀) (C^∞ with compact support ⊆ tsupport ψ, hence a test form on ℝ^{m+1}; ∂_sψ_s is a test form on ℝ^m by step 2). If q = j + 1 and φ is a dt-slice family of ψ on [0,1] (φ_s(x)(w) = ψ(cons(s,x))(e₀, ιw_1, …, ιw_j)), then for s ∈ [0,1] the chain rule (x ↦ cons(s,x) has derivative ι) gives Dφ_s(x)(v_i)(w) = Dψ(cons(s,x))(ιv_i)(e₀, ιw), so by exteriorDerivative_apply for φ_s the sum equals dφ_s(x)(v_1, …, v_q). Hence, for s ∈ [0,1] and a dt-slice family φ^{dψ} of dψ on [0,1]:
 (∗) φ^{dψ}_s = ∂_sψ_s − dφ_s (q = j + 1), φ^{dψ}_s = ∂_sψ_s (q = 0),
 as test forms on ℝ^m.

8. (Fundamental theorem of calculus.) Let M(X) < ∞ and g(s) := X(ψ_s). For every s and h ≠ 0, (ψ_{s+h} − ψ_s)/h − ∂_sψ_s is the horizontal slice (C2) of the form x ↦ [ψ(cons(s+h,x)) − ψ(cons(s,x))]/h − Dψ(cons(s,x))(e₀) = ∫_0^1 [Dψ(cons(s+τh,x)) − Dψ(cons(s,x))](e₀) dτ, whose operator norm is ≤ sup{‖Dψ(y) − Dψ(y′)‖ : |y − y′| ≤ |h|} → 0 as h → 0 (Dψ is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous); by (C2), (C3) and (R1), |(g(s+h) − g(s))/h − X(∂_sψ_s)| → 0. So g has derivative X(∂_sψ_s) at every s, and s ↦ X(∂_sψ_s) is continuous (step 3 applied to ψ′). By intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt, ∫_0^1 X(∂_sψ_s) ds = X(ψ_1) − X(ψ_0). If ψ₀, ψ₁ ∈ D^q(ℝ^m) satisfy the horizontal-slice identities of the statement at s = 0, 1, then ψ₀ = ψ_0 and ψ₁ = ψ_1 as test forms, so this equals X(ψ₁) − X(ψ₀).

9. (Boundary formulas, parts (II) and (III).) Let Z satisfy ProdChar(X, Z) with M(X) < ∞ (Z need not be the current of step 5). By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, ∂Z(ψ) = Z(exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ q ψ), whose underlying form is dψ. Let φ^{dψ} be a dt-slice family of dψ (R4). By ProdChar, ∂Z(ψ) = ∫_0^1 X(φ^{dψ}_s) ds. For q = 0, (∗) and step 8 give ∂Z(ψ) = ∫_0^1 X(∂_sψ_s) ds = X(ψ₁) − X(ψ₀): part (II). For q = j + 1 and a given dt-slice family φ of ψ on [0,1], (∗) and linearity of X give X(φ^{dψ}_s) = X(∂_sψ_s) − X(dφ_s) = X(∂_sψ_s) − ∂X(φ_s) for s ∈ [0,1] (boundary_apply). Both s ↦ X(∂_sψ_s) and s ↦ X(dφ_s) are continuous on [0,1]. The first is continuous by step 3 for the horizontal slices of ψ′. For the second, (∗) gives X(dφ_s) = X(∂_sψ_s) − X(φ^{dψ}_s) for s ∈ [0,1], and s ↦ X(φ^{dψ}_s) is continuous on [0,1] by step 3 applied to the dt-slice family φ^{dψ} of dψ. So the integral splits (intervalIntegral.integral_sub) and step 8 gives ∂Z(ψ) = X(ψ₁) − X(ψ₀) − ∫_0^1 ∂X(φ_s) ds: part (III).

10. (Normality; conjunct (f) of part (I).) Let Z be the current of step 5 and assume the HEq-normality hypothesis. Case k = 0: for ψ ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ 0 univ, take ψ₀, ψ₁ from step 2 (|ψ_i(x)| ≤ |ψ(cons(i,x))| ≤ 1 by (C2)); part (II) and (R1) give ∂Z(ψ) ≤ 2B, so M(∂Z) ≤ ofReal(2B) < ∞. Case k = j + 1: the hypothesis with Y := X (HEq.rfl) gives M(∂X) < ∞; put B′ := M(∂X).toReal. For ψ ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ (j+1) univ take ψ₀, ψ₁ (step 2) and a dt-slice family φ of ψ (R4), with |φ_s(x)| ≤ 1 (C1); part (III), (R1) for X and for ∂X give |∂Z(ψ)| ≤ B + B + ∫_0^1 B′ ds = 2B + B′, so M(∂Z) ≤ ofReal(2B + B′) < ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: Coefficient bounds: dt-slices and horizontal slices of a covector have Euclidean norm ≤ that of the covector; horizontal slices are test forms (compatible_form with j_s), dt-slices come from slice_forms.
s ↦ X(φ_s) is continuous on [0,1] by uniform continuity of η and |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖ (mass_bound).

Z(η) := ∫_0^1 X(φ^η_s)ds is linear and bounded by M(X)‖η‖, hence a current (test-form convergence forces sup norms to 0) with M(Z) ≤ M(X); ProdChar holds for every slice family, which also gives uniqueness.
spt Z ⊆ cyl(spt X): a form supported near a point off the closed cylinder has slices supported off spt X (vanish_off_support).
(dψ)^{(s)} = ∂_sψ_s − dφ_s from extDeriv_apply and the chain rule; s ↦ X(ψ_s) has derivative X(∂_sψ_s), so ∫_0^1 X(∂_sψ_s) = X(ψ_1) − X(ψ_0); ProdChar for dψ gives the boundary formulas.
Normality: the boundary formula and mass_bound give M(∂Z) ≤ 2M(X) + M(∂X).

subproblems.title: Products of integer multiplicity currents with [[0,1]] are integer multiplicity (Simon 3.2(2); supplied 3.5)
subproblems.statement: Notation: for s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m, cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι(v) := cons(0, v); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; for y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)); cyl(A) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1], tl(y) ∈ A}. D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q, M = mass, spt = support, ∂ = boundary. For X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) and Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), ProdChar(X, Z) means: for every η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and every φ : ℝ → D^k(ℝ^m) with φ(s)(x)(v_1, …, v_k) = η(cons(s, x))(e₀, ι(v_1), …, ι(v_k)) for all s ∈ [0,1], x ∈ ℝ^m, v ∈ (ℝ^m)^k (Fin.cons e₀ (ι ∘ v)), one has Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds (interval integral). For all m, k ∈ ℕ, every X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) and every Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}): if X is integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity X) and ProdChar(X, Z), then Z is integer multiplicity.

Source: item 3.5 of the supplied proof of deformation_pushforward_homotopy (Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(2); parent A4(d)): the product [[0,1]]×X of an integer multiplicity current X = τ(M, θ, ξ) is τ(M̃, θ̃, ξ̃) with M̃ = (0,1)×M, θ̃ = θ∘pr, ξ̃ = e₀∧ξ. Its sub-step 3.5(b) (the product formula H^{k+1}⌞(I×M) = L¹ × H^k⌞M) is supplied by the sibling hausdorff_product (dph_hausdorff_product_formula, whose frozen type is identical to that of the comparator-accepted iwl_cr_hausdorff_product_formula), whose statement is exactly that formula with I = ℝ together with the null-cylinder property; the remaining steps 3.5(a), (c), (d) are reproduced below. (The accepted declarations iwl_cr_ip_restrict_preimage_eq_map, iwl_cr_ip_pt_slab_restrict_eq_map, iwl_cr_ip_pt_cylinder_countablyRectifiable and iwl_cr_ip_slice_formula of another branch state individual steps below and may be reused by a later decomposition.)

Notation. As in the sibling interval_product: ℝ^p = Eucl p, e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1; cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)); ι(v) := cons(0, v) (linear isometry); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1; t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)), so y = cons(t(y), tl(y)) and |y|² = t(y)² + |tl(y)|². H^q := μHE[q]. For S ⊆ ℝ^m, cyl₀(S) := {y : tl(y) ∈ S} = cons(ℝ × S). |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ. A dt-slice family of η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) on [0,1] is φ : ℝ → D^k(ℝ^m) with φ_s(x)(v) = η(cons(s,x))(e₀, ιv_1, …, ιv_k) for s ∈ [0,1]; ProdChar(X, Z) is the hypothesis "Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ_s) ds for every η and every dt-slice family φ of η on [0,1]".
 Facts used (sibling dependencies): (R4) slice_forms (iwl_cr_ci_slice_testForm): every η has a dt-slice family φ^η (for all s ∈ ℝ). (R6) hausdorff_product (dph_hausdorff_product_formula): (R6a) H^k(N) = 0 ⇒ H^{k+1}(cyl₀(N)) = 0; (R6b) if A ⊆ ℝ^m is H^k-null-measurable, countably k-rectifiable and H^k(A ∩ K) < ∞ for all compact K, then for every Borel g : ℝ^{m+1} → [0, ∞], ∫⁻_{cyl₀(A)} g dH^{k+1} = ∫⁻_ℝ ∫⁻_A g(cons(s, x)) dH^k(x) ds.

Setup. X is integer multiplicity: there are M, θ, ξ with IsRectifiableTriple univ k M θ ξ, θ(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M, and X(ω) = tauAction k M θ ξ ω for all ω. Since θ > 0 on M, θ ≥ 1 on M. Let Π : Covector(ℝ^{m+1}, k+1) → Covector(ℝ^m, k), Π(γ)(v) := γ(e₀, ιv_1, …, ιv_k) (continuous linear: evaluation of the first argument at e₀ followed by pull-back by ι), with |Πγ| ≤ |γ| (the coefficient Πγ(e_I) is the coefficient of γ at the strictly increasing tuple (0, I_1+1, …, I_k+1), and I ↦ that tuple is injective). Define
 M̃ := {y : tl(y) ∈ M, t(y) ∈ Ioo 0 1}, θ̃(y) := θ(tl(y)), ξ̃(y) := ξ(tl(y)) ∘ Π ∈ NVector(ℝ^{m+1}, k+1)
(ξ̃ = Φ ∘ ξ ∘ tl with the continuous linear map Φ(w) := w.comp Π). We prove IsRectifiableTriple univ (k+1) M̃ θ̃ ξ̃ (steps 2–6), θ̃ ∈ ℕ on M̃ (obvious) and Z(η) = tauAction (k+1) M̃ θ̃ ξ̃ η for all η (step 7); this is IsIntegerMultiplicity Z.

1. (Product formula on slabs; consequences of R6.) (1a) M satisfies the hypotheses of (R6b): null-measurable and countably k-rectifiable by the triple, and H^k(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^k < ∞ for compact K (θ ≥ 1, IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K)). (1b) For a bounded open interval I and A as in (R6b), applying (R6b) to g·1_{t(·) ∈ I} gives ∫⁻_{cyl₀(A) ∩ {t ∈ I}} g dH^{k+1} = ∫⁻_I ∫⁻_A g(cons(s,x)) dH^k(x) ds. (1c) The identity persists for g ≥ 0 that agree on cyl₀(A) ∖ cyl₀(N) with a Borel g′ ≥ 0, for some H^k-null N ⊆ ℝ^m. Both sides of (1b) involve g only on cyl₀(A). The left side is unchanged because cyl₀(A) ∩ cyl₀(N) = cyl₀(A ∩ N) is H^{k+1}-null by (R6a). The right side is unchanged because for every s the functions x ↦ g(cons(s,x)) and x ↦ g′(cons(s,x)) agree on A ∖ N, while H^k(A ∩ N) = 0. (1d) Let g be a real function on cyl₀(A) ∩ {t ∈ I} with ∫|g| < ∞ which agrees on cyl₀(A) ∖ cyl₀(N) (N H^k-null) with a Borel function g′. Applying (1b)–(1c) to g⁺ and g⁻, which agree there with g′⁺ and g′⁻, gives ∫_{cyl₀(A)∩{t∈I}} g dH^{k+1} = ∫_I ∫_A g(cons(s,x)) dH^k(x) ds (Fubini; the inner integral is finite for a.e. s). Measurability of the iterated integrands: H^k⌞A is s-finite (A ∩ closedBall(0, n) has finite measure for every n), so for Borel g the maps s ↦ ∫⁻_A g(cons(s,x)) dH^k(x) are measurable (Measurable.lintegral_prod_right' for the product of volume and H^k⌞A, composed with the measurable map (s, x) ↦ cons(s, x)), and for integrable Borel g the map s ↦ ∫_A g(cons(s,x)) dH^k(x) is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right); this justifies the iterated integrals here and in steps 5c and 7.
 (1e) Measurable versions. θ is H^k⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (it is integrable on M ∩ closedBall(0,n) for every n, and M = ⋃_n M ∩ closedBall(0,n)), so there are a Borel θ′ and an H^k-null N₁ with θ = θ′ on M ∖ N₁; ξ is H^k⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (triple), so there are a strongly measurable ξ′ and an H^k-null N₂ with ξ = ξ′ on M ∖ N₂; and M is null-measurable, so there are a Borel M″ and an H^k-null N₃ ⊇ M Δ M″.

2. (Null-measurability and rectifiability of M̃.) cyl₀(M) Δ cyl₀(M″) = cyl₀(M Δ M″) ⊆ cyl₀(N₃) is H^{k+1}-null (R6a), and cyl₀(M″) is Borel (tl continuous); so cyl₀(M) is null-measurable and so is M̃ = cyl₀(M) ∩ {t ∈ Ioo 0 1}. By the triple, M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j with H^k(M₀) = 0 and F_j : ℝ^k → ℝ^m Lipschitz. Then M̃ ⊆ cyl₀(M₀) ∪ ⋃_j range G_j, where G_j : ℝ^{k+1} → ℝ^{m+1}, G_j(u) := cons(t(u), F_j(tl(u))) is Lipschitz (|G_j(u) − G_j(u′)|² = |t(u) − t(u′)|² + |F_j(tl u) − F_j(tl u′)|² ≤ max(1, Lip F_j)²|u − u′|²), and H^{k+1}(cyl₀(M₀)) = 0 (R6a). So M̃ is countably (k+1)-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable with exceptional set cyl₀(M₀)). M̃ ⊆ univ and θ̃ > 0 on M̃ are clear.

3. (Local integrability of θ̃.) Let K̃ be compact and K := tl(K̃) (compact). On M̃ ∩ K̃ we have θ̃ = θ(tl ·) with tl(·) ∈ M ∩ K and t(·) ∈ (0,1). θ̃ agrees on M̃ ∖ cyl₀(N₁) with the Borel θ′∘tl, and H^{k+1}(cyl₀(N₁)) = 0 by (R6a), so θ̃ is a.e.-strongly measurable on M̃, and by (1b)–(1c) with A = M ∩ K (which satisfies the hypotheses of R6b): ∫⁻_{M̃∩K̃} θ̃ dH^{k+1} ≤ ∫⁻_{(0,1)} ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH^k ds = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^k < ∞. Hence IntegrableOn θ̃ (M̃ ∩ K̃).

4. (Measurability of ξ̃.) ξ̃ agrees on M̃ ∖ cyl₀(N₂) with the strongly measurable Φ∘ξ′∘tl, and H^{k+1}(cyl₀(N₂)) = 0 (R6a); so ξ̃ is a.e.-strongly measurable w.r.t. H^{k+1}⌞M̃.

5. (Good points.) By the orientation field of the triple, the set N₄ of x ∈ M at which there is no orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^m with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x (span τ) and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ satisfies H^k(N₄) = 0 (restrict_apply for the null-measurable M). Hence M̃ ∖ cyl₀(M ∖ N₄) ⊆ cyl₀(N₄) is H^{k+1}-null (R6a). Fix y ∈ M̃ with x := tl(y) ∈ M ∖ N₄, t₀ := t(y) ∈ (0,1), and τ as above; put τ̃ := Fin.cons e₀ (ι ∘ τ) : Fin (k+1) → ℝ^{m+1}.
 (5a) τ̃ is orthonormal: |e₀| = 1, ⟨e₀, ιτ_i⟩ = 0, ⟨ιτ_i, ιτ_j⟩ = ⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩.
 (5b) ξ̃(y) = ±simpleNVector τ̃: for every γ, ξ̃(y)(γ) = ξ(x)(Πγ) = ±(Πγ)(τ_1, …, τ_k) = ±γ(e₀, ιτ_1, …, ιτ_k) = ±simpleNVector τ̃ (γ) (simpleNVector_apply), with the sign of ξ(x).
 (5c) HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt (k+1) M̃ θ̃ y (span τ̃). The dimension is k + 1 (orthonormal families are linearly independent). Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{m+1}) and R > 0 with f(y′) = 0 unless |t(y′)| ≤ R and |tl(y′)| ≤ R. For r > 0, blowUpMap y r '' M̃ = {(z − y)/r : z ∈ M̃} = {cons(s, x′) : s ∈ (−t₀/r, (1−t₀)/r), x′ ∈ M_r} with M_r := blowUpMap x r '' M (because (cons(s′, x″) − cons(t₀, x))/r = cons((s′ − t₀)/r, (x″ − x)/r)), and θ̃(y + r·cons(s, x′)) = θ(x + r x′). The set M_r satisfies the hypotheses of (R6b): it is the image of M under the similarity u ↦ (u − x)/r, which preserves null-measurability and countable rectifiability (compose the Lipschitz charts) and scales H^k by r^{−k}, so H^k(M_r ∩ K) = r^{−k}H^k(M ∩ (x + rK)) < ∞. Apply (1b)–(1d) with the following data: A := M_r; the bounded interval I_r := (−t₀/r, (1−t₀)/r); the H^k-null set N := blowUpMap x r '' N₁ (the image of a null set under a similarity); and the Borel function g′(z) := f(z)·θ′(x + r·tl(z)). On cyl₀(M_r) ∖ cyl₀(N), g′ agrees with the integrand f(z)θ̃(y + rz), because there tl(y + rz) = x + r·tl(z) ∈ M ∖ N₁. The integrability hypothesis of (1d) holds: by (1b)–(1c) for |g′|, the integral of |f(z)θ̃(y + rz)| over the blow-up is at most ‖f‖_∞·|I_r|·∫_{M_r ∩ closedBall(0,R)} θ(x + rx′) dH^k(x′) = ‖f‖_∞·|I_r|·r^{−k}∫_{M ∩ closedBall(x, rR)} θ dH^k, which is finite because θ is integrable on M ∩ closedBall(x, rR). The same replacement shows b_r(s) = ∫_{M_r} g′(cons(s, x′)) dH^k(x′) for every s, so s ↦ 1_{I_r}(s)·b_r(s) is measurable by (1d), as the dominated convergence below requires. This gives:
 ∫_{blowUpMap y r '' M̃} f(z)θ̃(y + rz) dH^{k+1}(z) = ∫_{−t₀/r}^{(1−t₀)/r} b_r(s) ds, b_r(s) := ∫_{M_r} f(cons(s, x′))θ(x + rx′) dH^k(x′).
 For each fixed s, f_s := f(cons(s, ·)) ∈ C_c(ℝ^m), and the hypothesis HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x (span τ) gives b_r(s) → θ(x)∫_{span τ} f_s dH^k as r → 0+. Domination: b_r(s) = 0 for |s| > R; |b_r(s)| ≤ ‖f‖_∞·β_r with β_r := ∫_{M_r} g₀(x′)θ(x + rx′) dH^k(x′), where g₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^m), 0 ≤ g₀ ≤ 1, g₀ = 1 on closedBall(0, R); the same hypothesis applied to g₀ gives β_r → θ(x)∫_{span τ} g₀ < ∞, so β_r ≤ B₀ for 0 < r < r₁. Moreover 1_{(−t₀/r, (1−t₀)/r)}(s) → 1 for every s as r → 0+ (t₀ ∈ (0,1)). By dominated convergence along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 (dominating function ‖f‖_∞B₀1_{[−R,R]}), the left side tends to ∫_ℝ θ(x)∫_{span τ} f(cons(s, v)) dH^k(v) ds. By (R6b) applied to A = span τ (a k-dimensional subspace: closed, countably k-rectifiable as the range of a linear isometry ℝ^k → span τ, locally H^k-finite) and the identity cyl₀(span τ) = ℝe₀ ⊕ ι(span τ) = span τ̃, this equals θ(x)∫_{span τ̃} f dH^{k+1} = θ̃(y)∫_{span τ̃} f dH^{k+1} (applied to f⁺ and f⁻). This is the defining limit of HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt (k+1) M̃ θ̃ y (span τ̃).
 Hence the orientation field holds for H^{k+1}-a.e. y ∈ M̃ (exceptional set ⊆ cyl₀(N₄)).

6. (Conclusion on the triple.) Steps 2–5 give all fields of IsRectifiableTriple univ (k+1) M̃ θ̃ ξ̃; θ̃(y) = θ(tl y) ∈ ℕ for y ∈ M̃.

7. (Action.) Let η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and φ := φ^η (R4). By ProdChar(X, Z), Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ_s) ds = ∫_0^1 ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(φ_s(x)) dH^k(x) ds. For s ∈ [0,1] and x ∈ M, φ_s(x) = Π(η(cons(s,x))), so θ(x)ξ(x)(φ_s(x)) = θ̃(cons(s,x))·ξ̃(cons(s,x))(η(cons(s,x))) =: F(cons(s,x)). Integrability: F vanishes unless tl(·) ∈ K := tl(tsupport η) (compact); for H^k-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ with τ orthonormal, and for any k-covector β and vectors with |τ_i| ≤ 1, |β(τ_1, …, τ_k)| ≤ m^{k/2}|β| (expand τ_i = Σ_a τ_i^a e_a: β(τ) = Σ_{J ∈ [m]^k} (Π_i τ_i^{J_i}) β(e_J), each |β(e_J)| ≤ |β| because it is ± a coefficient of β or 0, and Σ_J Π_i|τ_i^{J_i}| = Π_i Σ_a|τ_i^a| ≤ (√m)^k); hence |F(cons(s,x))| ≤ m^{k/2}·‖η‖_∞'·θ(x)1_K(x) with ‖η‖_∞' := sup_y |η(y)| (using |Πγ| ≤ |γ|), which is integrable over (0,1) × M by step 3; F agrees on cyl₀(M) ∖ cyl₀(N₁ ∪ N₂) with the Borel function y ↦ θ′(tl y)·Φ(ξ′(tl y))(η(y)), where Φ(w) := w.comp Π as in the setup. By (1d) with A = M and I = (0,1): ∫_{M̃} F dH^{k+1} = ∫_{(0,1)} ∫_M F(cons(s,x)) dH^k(x) ds, and the right side is ∫_0^1 X(φ_s) ds (interval integral over [0,1] = integral over (0,1)). Hence Z(η) = ∫_{M̃} θ̃(y)ξ̃(y)(η(y)) dH^{k+1}(y) = tauAction (k+1) M̃ θ̃ ξ̃ η.

By steps 6 and 7, Z is integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity with the triple (M̃, θ̃, ξ̃)). ∎

Source: Part 4 of the supplied proof of deformation_pushforward_homotopy (Simon Ch. 6, 2.25–2.27): 4.1 (push-forward of slices: j_s^#(G^#ω) = (G∘j_s)^#ω), 4.2 (homotopy formula (F_1)_#X − (F_0)_#X = ∂G_#([[0,1]]×X) + G_#([[0,1]]×∂X), via 2.5: d commutes with pull-back, and the boundary formula 3.4) and 4.3 (affine estimate |G_#([[0,1]]×X)(ψ)| ≤ c₁·s·L^k·M(X)·‖ψ‖, via the interior-product bound (F8) and the pull-back bound (F7)). Every push-forward G_#Y(ω) of the supplied proof is written here as Y(η) for a form η compatible with (G, ω) near the relevant set (2.2 of the supplied proof), so no push-forward current needs to be constructed: (E0)/(E1) say X(η₁) − X(η₀) = Z(η′) (+ Z′(θ′)), and (Aff) bounds |Z(η′)|.

Notation. As in the sibling interval_product: cons(s, x), ι, e₀, t(y), tl(y), j_s(x) = cons(s, x) (affine with derivative ι), cyl(A) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1], tl(y) ∈ A}; |γ| = covectorEuclideanNorm γ; dt-slice families and horizontal slices ψ_s(x)(v) := ψ(cons(s,x))(ιv_1, …, ιv_q); ProdChar(X, Z). "η is compatible with (g, ω) near A" means: there is an open N ⊇ A with η(x) = ω(g(x)).compContinuousLinearMap(Dg(x)) for x ∈ N (the hypotheses of the statement are of this form). Reused facts: (R1) mass_bound, (R2) vanish_off_support, (R3) compatible_form (iwl_sp_exists_compatible_testForm), (R4) slice_forms; sibling interval_product, parts (II) and (III) (boundary formulas for any Z with ProdChar(X, Z) and M(X) < ∞).

0. (Preliminaries.)
 (F2′) If T ∈ D_q(ℝ^p) and η, η′ ∈ D^q(ℝ^p) agree on an open N ⊇ spt T, then T(η) = T(η′): η − η′ vanishes on N, so tsupport(η − η′) ⊆ closure(ℝ^p ∖ N) = ℝ^p ∖ N, which is disjoint from spt T; (R2) and linearity give T(η) − T(η′) = 0.
 (S) spt ∂Y ⊆ spt Y for Y ∈ D_{q+1}(ℝ^p): if Y vanishes on all test forms supported in an open relatively compact W, so does ∂Y, because tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset); so the zero region of Y is contained in that of ∂Y.
 (Slice comparison) Let X ∈ D_q(ℝ^m), Z ∈ D_{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z), and let η, η′ ∈ D^{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) agree on an open Ñ ⊇ cyl(spt X). Then Z(η) = Z(η′). Indeed take dt-slice families φ, φ′ of η, η′ (R4); for s ∈ [0,1], φ_s and φ′_s agree on the open set {x : cons(s,x) ∈ Ñ} ⊇ spt X, so X(φ_s) = X(φ′_s) by (F2′), and ProdChar gives Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ_s) ds = ∫_0^1 X(φ′_s) ds = Z(η′).
 (Horizontal slices) For ψ ∈ D^q(ℝ^{m+1}) and s ∈ ℝ, the horizontal slice ψ_s is a test form on ℝ^m: apply (R3) with U = V = univ, A = univ, f = j_s (C^∞, proper because j_s is an isometric embedding); the resulting form equals ψ(j_s x)∘Dj_s(x) = ψ(cons(s,x))(ι·) everywhere.
 (Chain rule) For C^∞ G : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m′}, fderiv ℝ (fun x => G(cons(s,x))) x = (fderiv ℝ G (cons(s,x))).comp ι, i.e. D(G∘j_s)(x) = DG(cons(s,x))∘ι. This is fderiv_comp, since j_s(x) = s·e₀ + ι(x) is affine with derivative ι. Hence if θ is compatible with (G, ω) near cyl(spt X) on the open Ñ, then for s ∈ [0,1] the horizontal slice θ_s is compatible with (G∘j_s, ω) near spt X on the open set j_s⁻¹(Ñ) ⊇ spt X: θ_s(x)(v) = ω(G(cons(s,x)))(DG(cons(s,x))ιv_1, …) = ω((G∘j_s)(x))(D(G∘j_s)(x)v_1, …).
 (d and pull-back) If θ is compatible with (G, ω) near a set A on an open Ñ, then dθ is compatible with (G, dω) near A on Ñ: for y ∈ Ñ, θ and the C^∞ form G^#ω (y ↦ ω(G y)∘DG(y)) agree on the neighbourhood Ñ of y, so their exterior derivatives at y agree (exteriorDerivative = extDeriv is computed from fderiv, which only depends on the germ: Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq), and d(G^#ω)(y) = (dω)(G(y))∘DG(y) by Mathlib extDeriv_pullback (ω and G are C^∞).

1. (E0 and E1.) Let k = 0 (E0) or k = j + 1 (E1), and let X, Z (and Z′), G, ω, η₀, η₁, η′ (and θ′) be as in the statement; A := cyl(spt X) is closed and G is proper on A.
 (1a) By (R3) (U = V = univ) there is θ ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m+1}) compatible with (G, ω) near A, on an open Ñ ⊇ A.
 (1b) By (d and pull-back), dθ (= the form underlying exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k θ) is compatible with (G, dω) near A on Ñ. η′ is compatible with (G, dω) near A on some open Ñ′; so dθ = η′ on the open set Ñ ∩ Ñ′ ⊇ A, and (Slice comparison) gives Z(dθ) = Z(η′).
 (1c) By (Chain rule), θ_0 and η₀ are both compatible with (G∘j_0, ω) near spt X, so they agree on an open set containing spt X and X(θ_0) = X(η₀) (F2′); likewise X(θ_1) = X(η₁). (Here G∘j_s is the function fun x => G (cons s x) of the statement.)
 (1d) (E0) For k = 0, the boundary formula (II) of interval_product with ψ := θ, ψ₀ := θ_0, ψ₁ := θ_1 gives Z(dθ) = ∂Z(θ) = X(θ_1) − X(θ_0). With (1b), (1c): X(η₁) − X(η₀) = Z(η′).
 (1e) (E1) For k = j + 1, let φ be a dt-slice family of θ (R4). The boundary formula (III) of interval_product gives Z(dθ) = ∂Z(θ) = X(θ_1) − X(θ_0) − ∫_0^1 ∂X(φ_s) ds, and ProdChar(∂X, Z′) gives ∫_0^1 ∂X(φ_s) ds = Z′(θ). θ′ is compatible with (G, ω) near A on some open Ñ″, so θ = θ′ on Ñ ∩ Ñ″ ⊇ A ⊇ cyl(spt ∂X) (by (S)); (Slice comparison) for ∂X gives Z′(θ) = Z′(θ′). With (1b), (1c): X(η₁) − X(η₀) = Z(η′) + Z′(θ′).

2. (Interior-product and pull-back bounds.) Let c := c₁(m′, k) := √(m′^k)·√m′ ≥ 0.
 (F7) For a linear T : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} and a k-covector γ on ℝ^{m′}, |γ∘T| ≤ ‖T‖^k|γ|. Proof: for an alternating k-form β on ℝ^p, Σ_{I ∈ [p]^k} β(e_{I_1}, …, e_{I_k})² = k!·|β|² (tuples with a repeated index give 0; each strictly increasing tuple arises from k! orderings with the same square). One-slot bound: for a linear functional λ on ℝ^{m′}, Σ_a λ(Te_a)² = |Tᵀλ|² ≤ ‖T‖²|λ|² = ‖T‖²Σ_b λ(e_b)². Applying it successively to slots 1, …, k (the other slots fixed) gives Σ_{I ∈ [m]^k} γ(Te_{I_1}, …, Te_{I_k})² ≤ ‖T‖^{2k}Σ_{J ∈ [m′]^k} γ(e_{J_1}, …, e_{J_k})², i.e. k!|γ∘T|² ≤ ‖T‖^{2k}k!|γ|². (This is the accepted declaration iwl_sp_covectorEuclideanNorm_pullback_le of another branch, which a later decomposition may reuse.)
 (F8) For a (k+1)-covector γ on ℝ^{m′}, w ∈ ℝ^{m′} and linear T : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, the k-covector β(v) := γ(w, Tv_1, …, Tv_k) satisfies |β| ≤ c|w|‖T‖^k|γ|. Proof: β = γ_w∘T with γ_w(u) := γ(w, u_1, …, u_k). For strictly increasing J, γ_w(e_J) = Σ_i w_i γ(e_i, e_J), and γ(e_i, e_J) is 0 (if i ∈ J) or ± the coefficient of γ at the sorted tuple, so |γ(e_i, e_J)| ≤ |γ| and |γ_w(e_J)| ≤ Σ_i|w_i||γ| ≤ √m′|w||γ|; there are at most m′^k such J, so |γ_w| ≤ √(m′^k)√m′|w||γ|. Then (F7).

3. (Aff.) Let the data X, Z, F₀, F₁, O, s, L, B, ψ, C, η′ be as in the statement and G(y) := F₀(tl y) + t(y)·(F₁(tl y) − F₀(tl y)) (the map in the compatibility hypothesis; C^∞ since t, tl are linear and F₀, F₁ are C^∞).
 (3a) G is proper on A := cyl(spt X): for y ∈ A, tl(y) ∈ spt X ⊆ O and |G(y) − F₀(tl y)| = t(y)|F₁ − F₀|(tl y) ≤ s, so G⁻¹(K) ∩ A ⊆ cons([0,1] × (F₀⁻¹(cthickening s K) ∩ spt X)), a compact set (cthickening s K is compact in finite dimension and F₀ is proper on spt X); G⁻¹(K) ∩ A is closed, hence compact.
 (3b) Let U := {y : tl(y) ∈ O} (open, ⊇ A). (R3) with this U gives η̂ ∈ TestFormOn U (k+1), regarded as an element of D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) = TestFormOn univ (k+1) with the same underlying form (IsTestForm holds and tsupport ⊆ U ⊆ univ), and ζ with 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, η̂(y) = ζ(y)·ψ(G(y))∘DG(y) for all y, and η̂ compatible with (G, ψ) near A. Since η′ is also compatible near A, (Slice comparison) gives Z(η′) = Z(η̂).
 (3c) Let φ̂ be a dt-slice family of η̂ (R4). Fix s₀ ∈ [0,1] and x. If x ∉ O then cons(s₀, x) ∉ U, so η̂(cons(s₀,x)) = 0 and φ̂_{s₀}(x) = 0. If x ∈ O, put y := cons(s₀, x); then DG(y)e₀ = F₁(x) − F₀(x) =: w with |w| ≤ s, and DG(y)(ιv) = (1 − s₀)DF₀(x)v + s₀DF₁(x)v =: T v with ‖T‖ ≤ (1 − s₀)L + s₀L = L. So φ̂_{s₀}(x)(v) = ζ(y)·ψ(G(y))(w, Tv_1, …, Tv_k) and, by (F8), |φ̂_{s₀}(x)| ≤ c·s·L^k·|ψ(G(y))| ≤ c·s·L^k·C.
 (3d) By (R1) (W = univ, the bound B ≥ 0 on M(X)), |X(φ̂_{s₀})| ≤ B·c·s·L^k·C for s₀ ∈ [0,1]. By ProdChar, Z(η̂) = ∫_0^1 X(φ̂_{s₀}) ds₀, so (intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const, interval of length 1) |Z(η′)| = |Z(η̂)| ≤ c·s·L^k·B·C. The constant c = √(m′^k)·√m′ depends only on (m′, k). ∎
proof_key_steps: Locality: forms agreeing near spt X (resp. near cyl(spt X), via slices and ProdChar) have the same value under X (resp. Z).

Choose θ compatible with (G, ω) near cyl(spt X) (compatible_form); dθ is compatible with (G, dω) (extDeriv locality + extDeriv_pullback) and the horizontal slices θ_s are compatible with (G∘j_s, ω) near spt X (chain rule).
Boundary formula of interval_product: Z(dθ) = ∂Z(θ) = X(θ_1) − X(θ_0) (− ∫_0^1 ∂X(φ_s) = −Z′(θ) in degree j+1); replace θ_s, dθ, θ by η_i, η′, θ′ by locality.
Interior-product bound |γ(w, T·)| ≤ √(m′^k)√m′|w|‖T‖^k|γ| from coefficient counting and the pull-back bound |γ∘T| ≤ ‖T‖^k|γ|.

Affine estimate: with η̂ compatible with (G, ψ) and supported in {tl ∈ O} (compatible_form), the dt-slices satisfy |η̂^{(s)}(x)| ≤ c·s·L^k·C since DG e₀ = F₁ − F₀ and DG ι = (1−s)DF₀ + sDF₁; mass_bound and ProdChar give |Z(η′)| = |Z(η̂)| ≤ c·s·L^k·B·C.

Source: Part 5 of the supplied proof of deformation_pushforward_homotopy (Simon Ch. 6, 2.28–2.29): the push-forward of a normal current by a Lipschitz map as the limit of push-forwards by smooth approximations, 5.1 (existence and independence of the limit via the homotopy formula and the affine estimate 2.28), 5.2 (characterization by compatible forms), 5.3 (current), 5.4 (locality), 5.5 (mass with a local Lipschitz constant), 5.6 (support), 5.7 (boundary) and 5.8 (linearity in X). The characterization used here quantifies over all locally admissible approximations (smooth maps converging uniformly on an open set O ⊇ spt X with eventually bounded derivatives there); this builds the locality 5.4 of the supplied proof into the characterization, so no global extension of G enters the statement (the McShane extension is used only inside the sibling smooth_approx).

Notation. ℝ^p = Eucl p, e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1; D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q, M = mass, spt = support, ∂ = boundary, d = exteriorDerivative; |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ, ‖γ‖ the operator norm of a covector, ‖ω‖ := sup_y |ω(y)| for a test form ω; A_ρ := thickening ρ A. η is compatible with (g, ω) near A if η(x) = ω(g x).compContinuousLinearMap(Dg(x)) on an open set containing A. A triple (G_n, O, L) is a locally admissible sequence for (X, G) if O is open, spt X ⊆ O, every G_n is C^∞, eventually ‖DG_n(x)‖ ≤ L for all x ∈ O, and G_n → G uniformly on O. LipPF(X, G, S) is the property in the statement: for every locally admissible (G_n, O, L), every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) and every sequence η_n ∈ D^k(ℝ^m) eventually compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X, X(η_n) → S(ω). X is normal if M(X) < ∞ and, when k = q + 1, M(∂X) < ∞ (the HEq hypothesis of part (I), specialized to Y := X with HEq.rfl).
 Reused facts: (R1) mass_bound; (R2) vanish_off_support; (R3) compatible_form (iwl_sp_exists_compatible_testForm); siblings smooth_approx (N1, its statement (a)–(d)), interval_product (N2, part (I): for M(X) < ∞ the product Z with ProdChar(X, Z)), smooth_homotopy (N4: (E0), (E1), (Aff) with constant c(m, m′, k)). ProdChar is as in the statement of interval_product.

0. (Preliminaries, all proved here.)
 (F1′) If T ∈ D_q(ℝ^p) has M(T) < ∞ and |ω(x)| ≤ C for all x, then |T(ω)| ≤ M(T).toReal·C: (R1) with W = univ (mass = massOn univ) and B = M(T).toReal.
 (F2′) If T ∈ D_q(ℝ^p) and η, η′ ∈ D^q(ℝ^p) agree on an open N ⊇ spt T, then T(η) = T(η′): η − η′ vanishes on N, so tsupport(η − η′) ⊆ closure(ℝ^p ∖ N) = ℝ^p ∖ N is disjoint from spt T, and (R2) with linearity gives T(η) − T(η′) = T(η − η′) = 0. In particular a current with empty support is 0.
 (S) spt ∂Y ⊆ spt Y for Y ∈ D_{q+1}(ℝ^p): if Y vanishes on every test form supported in an open relatively compact W, so does ∂Y, since ∂Y(φ) = Y(dφ) and tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset); so the zero region of Y is contained in that of ∂Y.
 (F3c) If Y₂(ω) = aY(ω) + a₁Y₁(ω) for all ω, then spt Y₂ ⊆ spt Y ∪ spt Y₁: a point outside spt Y ∪ spt Y₁ has open relatively compact neighbourhoods W, W₁ on which Y, resp. Y₁, vanish, and Y₂ vanishes on the open relatively compact W ∩ W₁.
 (F5/F6) Current criterion. For a q-covector γ on ℝ^p, |γ| ≤ √(p^q)·‖γ‖ (operator norm): each coefficient |γ(e_I)| ≤ ‖γ‖·Π|e_{I_i}| = ‖γ‖ and there are at most p^q tuples. If TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 (all supports in one compact K, iteratedFDeriv ℝ i ω_j → 0 uniformly on K for every i), then for i = 0, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ = ‖ω_j x‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero) and ω_j = 0 off K, so ‖ω_j‖ := sup_x |ω_j(x)| → 0. Consequently, if T₀ : D^q(ℝ^{m′}) → ℝ is linear and |T₀(ω)| ≤ B‖ω‖ for all ω with B ≥ 0, then T₀ is sequentially continuous at 0 and defines S ∈ D_q(ℝ^{m′}) (toCurrent := T₀) with S(ω) = T₀(ω); for ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ q univ (|ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x) we get S(ω) ≤ B, so M(S) = sSup ofReal(S(ω)) ≤ ofReal B.
 (F7) Pull-back bound. For a linear T : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} and a k-covector γ on ℝ^{m′}, |γ∘T| ≤ ‖T‖^k|γ|, where (γ∘T)(v) := γ(Tv_1, …, Tv_k) (compContinuousLinearMap). Proof: for an alternating k-form β on ℝ^p, Σ_{I ∈ [p]^k} β(e_{I_1}, …, e_{I_k})² = k!·|β|² (tuples with a repeated index give 0; each strictly increasing tuple arises from exactly k! orderings with the same square). One-slot bound: for a linear functional λ on ℝ^{m′}, Σ_a λ(Te_a)² = |Tᵀλ|² ≤ ‖T‖²|λ|² = ‖T‖²Σ_b λ(e_b)². Applying it successively to the slots 1, …, k (the other slots fixed) gives Σ_{I ∈ [m]^k} γ(Te_{I_1}, …, Te_{I_k})² ≤ ‖T‖^{2k}Σ_{J ∈ [m′]^k} γ(e_{J_1}, …, e_{J_k})², i.e. k!|γ∘T|² ≤ ‖T‖^{2k}k!|γ|². (The accepted declaration iwl_sp_covectorEuclideanNorm_pullback_le of another branch states exactly this and may be reused by a later decomposition.)
 (CF) Compatible forms with support control. If g : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} is C^∞, F ⊆ ℝ^m is closed, g⁻¹(K) ∩ F is compact for every compact K, and U ⊇ F is open, then for every ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^{m′}) there is η ∈ D^q(ℝ^m) compatible with (g, ω) near F, with η = 0 off U and |η(x)| ≤ ‖Dg(x)‖^q|ω(g x)| for all x: apply (R3) with this U (and V = univ) to get η ∈ TestFormOn U q (so tsupport η ⊆ U) and ζ with 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 and η(x) = ζ(x)·ω(g x)∘Dg(x); regard η as an element of D^q(ℝ^m) (same underlying form); then use (F7).
 (dP) d and pull-back. If θ is compatible with (g, φ) near F on an open N, then dθ (the form underlying exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ q θ) is compatible with (g, dφ) near F on N: for x ∈ N, θ and the C^∞ form g^#φ (x′ ↦ φ(g x′)∘Dg(x′)) agree on the neighbourhood N of x, so their exterior derivatives at x agree (exteriorDerivative = extDeriv is computed from fderiv, which only depends on the germ: Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq), and d(g^#φ)(x) = (dφ)(g x)∘Dg(x) by Mathlib extDeriv_pullback (φ and g are C^∞).
 (P) Properness transfer. If G is proper on a closed F (G⁻¹(K) ∩ F compact for compact K) and |G_n − G| ≤ d on F, then G_n is proper on F: G_n⁻¹(K) ∩ F is closed (G_n continuous, F closed) and contained in the compact G⁻¹(cthickening d K) ∩ F. If moreover |G′_n − G| ≤ d on F, the affine homotopy H_n(y) := G_n(tl y) + t(y)·(G′_n(tl y) − G_n(tl y)) — which is C^∞ when G_n, G′_n are, because t and tl are continuous linear maps — is proper on cyl(F) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1], tl(y) ∈ F}: for such y, |H_n(y) − G(tl y)| ≤ d, so H_n⁻¹(K) ∩ cyl(F) is a closed subset of the compact cons([0,1] × (G⁻¹(cthickening d K) ∩ F)). Here t(y), tl(y), cons(s, x) are as in the sibling interval_product statement, t(cons(s,x)) = s and tl(cons(s,x)) = x, so H_n(cons(0,x)) = G_n(x) and H_n(cons(1,x)) = G′_n(x).

1. (Comparison lemma.) Let X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) be normal, G proper on spt X, (G_n, O, L) and (G′_n, O′, L′) locally admissible for (X, G), ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}), and η_n, η′_n eventually compatible with (G_n, ω), (G′_n, ω) near spt X. Then X(η′_n) − X(η_n) → 0.
 Proof. O″ := O ∩ O′ is open and contains spt X; L″ := max(max(L, L′), 0); eventually ‖DG_n‖, ‖DG′_n‖ ≤ L″ on O″. Let ε > 0. Eventually |G_n − G| ≤ ε and |G′_n − G| ≤ ε on O″, so |G′_n − G_n| ≤ 2ε on O″; by (P) (F = spt X) G_n is proper on spt X and H_n (the affine homotopy from G_n at t = 0 to G′_n at t = 1) is proper on cyl(spt X). Note H_n∘j_0 = G_n and H_n∘j_1 = G′_n (t(cons(s,x)) = s, tl(cons(s,x)) = x), so η_n, η′_n are compatible with (H_n∘j_0, ω), (H_n∘j_1, ω) near spt X. Let Z be the product of X (N2 (I)).
 Case k = 0: choose (R3) η̃_n compatible with (H_n, dω) near cyl(spt X). (E0): X(η′_n) − X(η_n) = Z(η̃_n). (Aff) with F₀ = G_n, F₁ = G′_n, O″, s = 2ε, L″, B = M(X).toReal, ψ = dω, C = ‖dω‖: |Z(η̃_n)| ≤ c·2ε·B·‖dω‖.
 Case k = q + 1: M(∂X) < ∞; let Z′ be the product of ∂X (N2 (I) for ∂X). Choose η̃_n, θ̃_n compatible with (H_n, dω), (H_n, ω) near cyl(spt X) (R3). (E1): X(η′_n) − X(η_n) = Z(η̃_n) + Z′(θ̃_n). (Aff) for (X, Z, dω) gives |Z(η̃_n)| ≤ c·2ε·L″^{q+1}·M(X).toReal·‖dω‖; (Aff) for (∂X, Z′, ω) — note spt ∂X ⊆ spt X ⊆ O″ by (S), G_n is proper on the closed subset spt ∂X of spt X, and θ̃_n is compatible near cyl(spt X) ⊇ cyl(spt ∂X) — gives |Z′(θ̃_n)| ≤ c′·2ε·L″^q·M(∂X).toReal·‖ω‖.
 In both cases limsup_n |X(η′_n) − X(η_n)| ≤ C₀ε with C₀ independent of ε; as ε > 0 is arbitrary, the difference tends to 0. ∎(1)

2. (Reference sequence.) Assume the hypotheses of part (I). Apply smooth_approx (N1) with A := spt X and δ := r: there are Ĝ (Lipschitz, Ĝ = G on (spt X)_r) and C^∞ maps G_n with G_n → Ĝ uniformly on ℝ^m and ‖DG_n(x)‖ ≤ Λ for x ∈ O₀ := (spt X)_{r/2}. Since Ĝ = G on O₀ ⊆ (spt X)_r, (G_n, O₀, Λ) is locally admissible for (X, G). Choose n₀ with |G_n − G| ≤ 1 on O₀ for n ≥ n₀; by (P) G_n is proper on spt X for n ≥ n₀. For n ≥ n₀ and each ω let η_n(ω) be a compatible form for (G_n, ω) near spt X with support control U := O₀ ((CF), F := spt X): η_n(ω) = 0 off O₀ and |η_n(ω)(x)| ≤ Λ^k|ω(G_n x)| ≤ Λ^k‖ω‖. For n < n₀ put η_n(ω) := 0.

3. (Existence of the limit.) For fixed ω the real sequence a_n := X(η_n(ω)) is Cauchy: otherwise there are ε > 0 and indices p_i, n_i → ∞ with |a_{p_i} − a_{n_i}| ≥ ε; but (G_{p_i}, O₀, Λ) and (G_{n_i}, O₀, Λ) are locally admissible for (X, G) (subsequences of a uniformly convergent sequence), with eventually compatible forms η_{p_i}(ω), η_{n_i}(ω), so step 1 gives a_{p_i} − a_{n_i} → 0, a contradiction. Let S₀(ω) := lim_n X(η_n(ω)).
 Linearity: for n ≥ n₀, aη_n(ω) + bη_n(ω′) and η_n(aω + bω′) are both compatible with (G_n, aω + bω′) near spt X, so by (F2′) X(η_n(aω + bω′)) = aX(η_n(ω)) + bX(η_n(ω′)); pass to the limit.
 Bound: by (R1) (W = univ, B = M(X).toReal, C = Λ^k‖ω‖), |X(η_n(ω))| ≤ Λ^kM(X).toReal‖ω‖, hence |S₀(ω)| ≤ Λ^kM(X).toReal‖ω‖. By (F5/F6) there is S ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) with S(ω) = S₀(ω) for all ω and M(S) ≤ ofReal(Λ^kM(X).toReal) = (Λ : ℝ≥0∞)^k·M(X) (M(X) < ∞): the mass conjunct.

4. (LipPF(X, G, S).) Let (G′_n, O′, L′) be locally admissible for (X, G), ω given and η′_n eventually compatible with (G′_n, ω). By step 1 applied to (G_n, O₀, Λ), η_n(ω) and (G′_n, O′, L′), η′_n: X(η′_n) − X(η_n(ω)) → 0; and X(η_n(ω)) → S(ω). Hence X(η′_n) → S(ω).

5. (Uniqueness.) If LipPF(X, G, S′), apply it to (G_n, O₀, Λ) and η_n(ω): X(η_n(ω)) → S′(ω); also → S(ω). So S′(ω) = S(ω) for all ω and S′ = S (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).

6. (Support.) Let y₀ ∉ closure(G(spt X)); choose ρ > 0 with closedBall(y₀, 2ρ) ∩ closure(G(spt X)) = ∅ and put W := ball(y₀, ρ). Let ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W and K := tsupport ω (compact). For z ∈ K and x ∈ spt X, |G(x) − z| ≥ |G(x) − y₀| − |y₀ − z| > 2ρ − ρ = ρ. For n large, |G_n − G| < ρ on spt X ⊆ O₀, so G_n(spt X) ∩ K = ∅. The set N_n := G_n⁻¹(ℝ^{m′} ∖ K) is open and contains spt X, and for x ∈ N_n, ω(G_n x) = 0, so the zero form is compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X. By step 4 (with η′_n := 0), S(ω) = lim X(0) = 0. Thus S vanishes on the open relatively compact W, y₀ lies in the zero region, and y₀ ∉ spt S. Hence spt S ⊆ closure(G(spt X)).

7. (Part (II): boundary.) Let X ∈ D_{q+1}(ℝ^m) with M(X), M(∂X) < ∞, G, Λ, r as stated and S with LipPF(X, G, S). ∂X ∈ D_q is normal (M(∂X) < ∞; if q = q′ + 1, ∂∂X = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary) has mass 0), spt ∂X ⊆ spt X (S), so G is Λ-Lipschitz on (spt ∂X)_r and proper on spt ∂X. By part (I) there is S_∂ with LipPF(∂X, G, S_∂). Let φ ∈ D^q(ℝ^{m′}). With the reference sequence of step 2 for X (also locally admissible for (∂X, G), as O₀ ⊇ spt X ⊇ spt ∂X), choose for n ≥ n₀ a form θ_n compatible with (G_n, φ) near spt X (R3). θ_n is compatible near spt ∂X, so ∂X(θ_n) → S_∂(φ). By (dP), dθ_n is compatible with (G_n, dφ) near spt X, so ∂X(θ_n) = X(dθ_n) → S(dφ) = ∂S(φ) (boundary_apply). Hence S_∂(φ) = ∂S(φ) for all φ, S_∂ = ∂S, and LipPF(∂X, G, ∂S) holds.

8. (Part (III): linearity.) F := spt X ∪ spt X₁ is closed, G is Λ-Lipschitz on F_r and proper on F, and spt X₂ ⊆ F by (F3c). smooth_approx with A := F, δ := r gives C^∞ maps G_n with ‖DG_n‖ ≤ Λ on O_F := F_{r/2} and G_n → G uniformly on O_F; (G_n, O_F, Λ) is locally admissible for (X, G), (X₁, G) and (X₂, G) (each support lies in F ⊆ O_F). Fix ω. For n large, G_n is proper on F (P), and (R3) gives η_n compatible with (G_n, ω) near F, hence near spt X, spt X₁ and spt X₂. Then X₂(η_n) = aX(η_n) + a₁X₁(η_n), and the three sequences converge to S₂(ω), S(ω), S₁(ω) by LipPF(X₂, G, S₂), LipPF(X, G, S), LipPF(X₁, G, S₁). Hence S₂(ω) = aS(ω) + a₁S₁(ω). ∎
proof_key_steps: Comparison lemma: two locally admissible approximations give asymptotically equal X(η_n) — (E0)/(E1) for the affine homotopy H_n between them and (Aff) on O ∩ O′ bound the difference by C₀·sup|G′_n − G_n|.
Reference sequence from smooth_approx on (spt X)_{r/2} with ‖DG_n‖ ≤ Λ; compatible forms with support in (spt X)_{r/2} (compatible_form).
X(η_n(ω)) is Cauchy (comparison along subsequences); the limit is linear (locality) and bounded by Λ^kM(X)‖ω‖, hence a current S with M(S) ≤ Λ^kM(X).
LipPF(X, G, S) and uniqueness by the comparison lemma; support: η_n = 0 is compatible once G_n(spt X) misses tsupport ω.
Boundary: dθ_n is compatible with (G_n, dφ), so ∂X(θ_n) = X(dθ_n) → ∂S(φ), identifying the push-forward of ∂X given by (I) with ∂S.
Linearity: one approximation and one compatible form near spt X ∪ spt X₁ serve X, X₁, X₂.

Source: items 2.6 (rectifiable representation of smooth push-forwards: g_#X(ω) = X(η) = ∫_M θ⟨ω(g(x)), Dg(x)_#ξ(x)⟩ dH^k, using H^k(M ∖ spt X) = 0) and 5.9 (integrality of Lipschitz push-forwards through the premise (S5′); parent I.7) of the supplied proof of deformation_pushforward_homotopy. The premise (S5′) of this child is verbatim the premise of the parent statement (the conclusion of the sibling deformation_im_pushforward_limit after its premise LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity).

Notation. As in the sibling lipschitz_pushforward: locally admissible sequences (G_n, O, L) and the property LipPF(X, G, S) of the statement; A_ρ := thickening ρ A; H^k := μHE[k]. Reused facts: (R3) compatible_form (iwl_sp_exists_compatible_testForm); (R5) support_null (iwl_sp_rectifiable_support_null): if IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ and T(ω) = tauAction k M θ ξ ω for all ω, then H^k(M ∖ spt T) = 0; sibling smooth_approx (N1).

1. (Representation.) X is integer multiplicity: there are M, θ, ξ with IsRectifiableTriple univ k M θ ξ, θ(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M (as ∃ j : ℕ, θ x = j) and X(ω) = tauAction k M θ ξ ω for all ω.

2. (Approximations.) Apply smooth_approx (N1) with A := spt X and δ := r: there are Ĝ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, L ≥ 0 and maps G_n with Ĝ L-Lipschitz, Ĝ = G on (spt X)_r, each G_n C^∞ and L-Lipschitz, G_n → Ĝ uniformly on ℝ^m, and ‖DG_n(x)‖ ≤ Λ for x ∈ O₀ := (spt X)_{r/2}. Since Ĝ = G on O₀, (G_n, O₀, Λ) is locally admissible for (X, G) (O₀ open, spt X ⊆ O₀, uniform convergence to G on O₀).

3. (Apply (S5′).) Ĝ is L-Lipschitz, and Ĝ⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X = G⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X is compact for compact K (Ĝ = G on spt X ⊆ (spt X)_r). Applying (S5′) to P := m, Q := m′, k, X, (M, θ, ξ), g := Ĝ, Λ := L gives S′ ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) with IsIntegerMultiplicity S′ and: for every sequence (g_n) of C¹ maps with a common Lipschitz bound converging uniformly to Ĝ and every ω, ∫_M θ(x)·nVectorPushforward k (Dg_n(x)) (ξ(x)) (ω(g_n x)) dH^k(x) → S′(ω). Take g_n := G_n: C^∞ implies C¹ (ContDiff.of_le), the common Lipschitz bound is L, and G_n → Ĝ uniformly. Hence for every ω:
 (∗) I_n(ω) := ∫_M θ(x)·nVectorPushforward k (DG_n(x)) (ξ(x)) (ω(G_n x)) dH^k(x) → S′(ω).

4. (Rectifiable formula, 2.6.) Choose n₀ with |G_n − G| ≤ 1 on spt X for n ≥ n₀ (uniform convergence on O₀ ⊇ spt X). For n ≥ n₀, G_n is proper on spt X (G_n⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X is closed and contained in the compact G⁻¹(cthickening 1 K) ∩ spt X), so (R3) (U = V = univ, A = spt X) gives, for each ω, a form η_n ∈ D^k(ℝ^m) compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X, on an open N_n ⊇ spt X. By (R5), H^k(M ∖ spt X) = 0, so for H^k-a.e. x ∈ M we have x ∈ spt X ⊆ N_n and
 η_n(x) = ω(G_n x).compContinuousLinearMap(DG_n(x)) = covectorPullback k (DG_n(x)) (ω(G_n x)),
 hence ξ(x)(η_n(x)) = (ξ(x) ∘ covectorPullback k (DG_n(x)))(ω(G_n x)) = nVectorPushforward k (DG_n(x)) (ξ(x)) (ω(G_n x)) by the definition nVectorPushforward k L w = w.comp (covectorPullback k L). Therefore (integral_congr_ae for the measure H^k⌞M)
 X(η_n) = tauAction k M θ ξ η_n = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(η_n(x)) dH^k(x) = I_n(ω) (n ≥ n₀).

5. (Identification.) For n ≥ n₀ the η_n are compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X, so LipPF(X, G, S) applied to the locally admissible (G_n, O₀, Λ) gives X(η_n) → S(ω) (set η_n := 0 for n < n₀; compatibility is only required eventually). By step 4 and (∗), X(η_n) = I_n(ω) → S′(ω). Limits in ℝ are unique, so S(ω) = S′(ω) for all ω, S = S′ (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), and S is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: smooth_approx on (spt X)_r gives a Lipschitz extension Ĝ and C^∞ maps G_n → Ĝ uniformly with a common Lipschitz bound and ‖DG_n‖ ≤ Λ near spt X; they are locally admissible for (X, G).
(S5′) for (X, M, θ, ξ, Ĝ) gives an integer multiplicity S′ with ∫_M θ⟨ω(G_n), DG_n#ξ⟩ dH^k → S′(ω).
2.6: for η_n compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X, X(η_n) equals that integral because H^k(M ∖ spt X) = 0 (support_null) and ξ(η_n) = nVectorPushforward k (DG_n) ξ (ω∘G_n) on spt X.
LipPF gives X(η_n) → S(ω); hence S = S′ is integer multiplicity.

Source: parent proof Step 2 (basic mass estimate). It is stated with an explicit real bound B for M_W(T) and an explicit pointwise bound C for |ω|, which avoids dividing by sup|ω| and any case distinction on ω = 0.

Notation: for an n-covector α, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P, I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}, where e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i. M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(T(ψ)) over ψ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W = {ψ ∈ TestFormOn U n : tsupport ψ ⊆ W and |ψ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}.

1. (Homogeneity.) For t ∈ ℝ and a covector α, |tα| = |t|·|α|. Each coefficient satisfies (tα)(e_I) = t·α(e_I), so the sum of squares is multiplied by t², and √(t²S) = |t|·√S.
2. (C ≥ 0.) 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ C.
3. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix a real c > C, so c > 0. Let s ∈ {c⁻¹, −c⁻¹}. TestFormOn U n is a real submodule, so s•ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Also tsupport(s•ω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, and by Step 1, |(s•ω)(x)| = c⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ C/c ≤ 1 for every x. Hence s•ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, and GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn gives ENNReal.ofReal(T(s•ω)) ≤ M_W(T) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B.
4. (Unpacking.) Because B ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B implies a ≤ B (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff). By linearity T(s•ω) = s·T(ω). Therefore c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B and −c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B. Multiplying by c > 0 gives T(ω) ≤ Bc and −T(ω) ≤ Bc, i.e. |T(ω)| ≤ B·c. This holds for every c > C.
5. (Letting c ↓ C.) Let ε > 0 and c := C + ε/(B+1) > C. Step 4 gives |T(ω)| ≤ BC + Bε/(B+1) ≤ BC + ε. Since ε > 0 is arbitrary, |T(ω)| ≤ B·C (le_of_forall_pos_le_add). ∎
proof_key_steps: |tα| = |t|·|α| and C ≥ 0.
For c > C, ±c⁻¹ω is mass-admissible for W, so ±c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B by le_massOn and B ≥ 0.
Hence |T(ω)| ≤ B·c for every c > C; let c decrease to C.

Source: the parenthetical argument in Step 1 of the parent proof ("a test form supported in the open zero region is annihilated: cover its compact support by finitely many open sets on which T vanishes and use a partition of unity"), with Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T), written out for the exact SimonGMT definitions.

Notation. For T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, `T.VanishesOn W` means T(η) = 0 for every η ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport η ⊆ W. Let 𝒲 be the family of all W ⊆ ℝ^P with W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W. By definition T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲 and T.support = U ∖ T.zeroRegion.

1. Let K := tsupport ω. Since ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, ω is C^∞, has compact support (so K is compact, in particular closed) and K ⊆ U.
2. K ⊆ ⋃𝒲. Let x ∈ K. Then x ∈ U, and x ∉ T.support by the disjointness hypothesis, i.e. x ∉ U ∖ T.zeroRegion; hence x ∈ T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲.
3. Every member of 𝒲 is open, so by compactness of K there are finitely many W_1, …, W_r ∈ 𝒲 (r ≥ 0; r = 0 when K = ∅) with K ⊆ W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_r (e.g. `IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover_image`; it is convenient to index the cover by the resulting finite subfamily rather than by Fin r).
4. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), with the model with corners 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), is a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, σ-compact smooth manifold, and K is closed and covered by the open sets W_i (i ranging over the finite index set of step 3). Hence there is a smooth partition of unity on K subordinate to (W_i): C^∞ functions ψ_1, …, ψ_r : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for every i and Σ_i ψ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∈ K (Mathlib `SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate`; a real-valued `ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P) 𝓘(ℝ)` function of class C^∞ is `ContDiff ℝ ∞` by `contMDiff_iff_contDiff`).
5. For each i put η_i(x) := ψ_i(x) • ω(x). Then η_i is C^∞ (a C^∞ scalar function times a C^∞ form). If ω(x) = 0 or ψ_i(x) = 0 then η_i(x) = 0, so support η_i ⊆ support ω ∩ support ψ_i; taking closures, tsupport η_i ⊆ K ∩ tsupport ψ_i ⊆ U ∩ W_i. In particular η_i has compact support (closed subset of the compact K). Thus η_i ∈ TestFormOn U n and tsupport η_i ⊆ W_i.
6. Since W_i ∈ 𝒲, T vanishes on W_i, so T(η_i) = 0 for every i.
7. ω = Σ_i η_i in TestFormOn U n (checked pointwise). If x ∈ K, then Σ_i ψ_i(x) • ω(x) = (Σ_i ψ_i(x)) • ω(x) = ω(x). If x ∉ K, then x ∉ support ω, so ω(x) = 0 and every η_i(x) = 0. (If r = 0 then K = ∅, ω = 0 and both sides are 0.)
8. T acts ℝ-linearly on TestFormOn U n (T.toCurrent is a linear map), so by steps 6 and 7, T(ω) = Σ_i T(η_i) = 0.
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of U disjoint from spt T, hence contained in the zero region, i.e. covered by the open sets W on which T vanishes.
Extract a finite subcover W_1, …, W_r of tsupport ω.
Take a smooth partition of unity ψ_1, …, ψ_r on tsupport ω subordinate to the W_i (Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate).
Each ψ_i • ω is a test form in U with tsupport in W_i, so T(ψ_i • ω) = 0.
ω = Σ_i ψ_i • ω pointwise, so T(ω) = 0 by linearity.

Notation: p(x) := Df(x)^#(ω(f(x))) = (ω(f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) is the pull-back form f^#ω. C^∞ means smoothness of order ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), i.e. of every finite order.

1. (The compact set.) ω ∈ D^j(V) has compact support, so tsupport ω is compact (HasCompactSupport.isCompact), and tsupport ω ⊆ V. By the properness hypothesis, K := f⁻¹(tsupport ω) ∩ A is compact, and K ⊆ A ⊆ U.
2. (Thickenings.) K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U, so there is δ₀ > 0 with cthickening δ₀ K ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Define:
   - O := thickening (δ₀/2) K, open, with K ⊆ O (self_subset_thickening, as δ₀/2 > 0);
   - C := cthickening (δ₀/2) K, closed, with O ⊆ C (thickening_subset_cthickening);
   - s := thickening δ₀ K, open, with C ⊆ s (cthickening_subset_thickening', since 0 < δ₀ and δ₀/2 < δ₀).
   If K = ∅, all these sets are empty and the argument below still applies.
3. (The cut-off.) Smooth Urysohn (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff with n = ⊤, applied to the open set s and the closed set C ⊆ s) gives a C^∞ function ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ with range ζ ⊆ [0, 1], support ζ = s, and ζ(x) = 1 ⟺ x ∈ C. Consequently:
   - 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 everywhere, and ζ = 1 on O;
   - tsupport ζ = closure s ⊆ cthickening δ₀ K ⊆ U (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening);
   - cthickening δ₀ K is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^P is proper), so its closed subset tsupport ζ is compact, i.e. ζ has compact support.
4. (p is C^∞.)
   - x ↦ Df(x) is C^∞ because f is C^∞ (ContDiff.fderiv_right, using ∞ + 1 ≤ ∞).
   - x ↦ ω(f(x)) is C^∞ as the composition of the C^∞ maps ω (a test form) and f.
   - B ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM B is C^∞. It sends a continuous linear map B : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q to the continuous linear map α ↦ α.compContinuousLinearMap B on j-covectors, and it is analytic on the whole space (ContinuousAlternatingMap.analyticOnNhd_compContinuousLinearMapCLM), hence C^∞ (AnalyticOnNhd.contDiff).

   0 = T(ω_φ) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(φ(x)·b) dμ(x) = ∫ φ(x)·g_b(x) dν(x).
6. (Fundamental lemma.) Steps 4 and 5 are exactly the hypotheses of IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero for the open set W, the measure ν and the function g_b. Hence for ν-a.e. x: x ∈ W ⟹ θ(x)·ξ(x)(b) = 0. Since θ(x) > 0 at good points, for ν-a.e. x: x ∈ W ⟹ ξ(x)(b) = 0.

Part (a). Let N ⊆ E with H^m(N) = 0. We show H^{m+1}(N̂) = 0.
1. (m = 0.) μHE[0] = μH[0] and μH[0]({x}) = 1 for every x (L7). So H^0(N) = 0 forces N = ∅, and then N̂ = ∅.
2. (m ≥ 1: what suffices.) N̂ = ⋃_{a ∈ ℤ} Φ([a, a+1] × N), so by countable subadditivity it suffices to show μH[m+1](Φ([a, a+1] × N)) = 0 for each a ∈ ℤ.
   - By hausdorffMeasure_apply, μH[m+1](S) = sup_{r>0} inf Σ_n diam(t_n)^{m+1}, the infimum over countable covers (t_n) of S with diam t_n ≤ r. (For m + 1 ≥ 1 the factor ⨆_{t_n ≠ ∅} is harmless because diam ∅ = 0.)
   - So it suffices: for every r > 0 and ε′ > 0, Φ([a, a+1] × N) has a countable cover by sets of diameter ≤ r with Σ diam^{m+1} ≤ ε′.
   - Given r, fix δ ∈ (0, 1) with √2·δ ≤ r. Steps 3–4 produce, for every ε ∈ (0, (δ/2)^m), such a cover with diameters ≤ √2·δ and Σ diam^{m+1} ≤ 2^{2+(m+1)/2}·ε.
3. (Covering N.) Since μH[m](N) = 0, the infimum in hausdorffMeasure_apply for the radius δ/2 is 0. So there are sets C_i (i ∈ ℕ) with N ⊆ ⋃_i C_i, diam C_i ≤ δ/2 and Σ_i (diam C_i)^m < ε. (Because m ≥ 1, (diam ∅)^m = 0^m = 0, so the factor ⨆_{C_i ≠ ∅} can be dropped. All diameters here are finite, so ediam = diam.)
   - Put d_i := max(diam C_i, (ε·2^{−i−1})^{1/m}).
   - Then 0 < d_i ≤ max(δ/2, ε^{1/m}) < δ < 1, and d_i^m ≤ (diam C_i)^m + ε·2^{−i−1}, so Σ_i d_i^m < 2ε.
4. (Covering the strip.) Let k_i := ⌈1/d_i⌉ ≤ 1/d_i + 1 ≤ 2/d_i.
   - [a, a+1] ⊆ ⋃_{k=0}^{k_i−1} [a + k·d_i, a + (k+1)·d_i], so Φ([a, a+1] × C_i) ⊆ ⋃_{k<k_i} Q_{i,k} with Q_{i,k} := Φ([a + k·d_i, a + (k+1)·d_i] × C_i).
   - By the distance formula, diam Q_{i,k} ≤ √(d_i² + (diam C_i)²) ≤ √2·d_i < √2·δ.
   - The countable family (Q_{i,k}) covers Φ([a, a+1] × N), and Σ_{i,k} (diam Q_{i,k})^{m+1} ≤ Σ_i (2/d_i)(√2·d_i)^{m+1} = 2^{1+(m+1)/2}·Σ_i d_i^m ≤ 2^{2+(m+1)/2}·ε.
   - To apply hausdorffMeasure_apply, index the family by ℕ: send n to Q_{i,k} if n = Nat.pair i k with k < k_i, and to ∅ otherwise. Empty sets contribute 0 because of the factor ⨆_{t_n ≠ ∅}.
   - By Step 2, μH[m+1](Φ([a, a+1] × N)) = 0 for every a, hence H^{m+1}(N̂) = 0.

Part (b). Let A be as in (b) and g : E′ → [0, ∞] measurable.
For B ⊆ E and s ∈ ℝ write:
- LHS(B) := ∫⁻_{B̂} g dH^{m+1};
- φ_B(s) := ∫⁻_{x ∈ B} g(Φ(s,x)) dH^m(x);
- RHS(B) := ∫⁻_ℝ φ_B(s) ds.
The goal is LHS(A) = RHS(A). The function (s, x) ↦ g(Φ(s,x)) is Borel on ℝ × E (Φ is continuous).

5. (Reduction to Borel A.) By NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq there is a Borel A₀ ⊆ A with H^m(A ∖ A₀) = 0.

   - Then H^m⌞A is σ-finite: E = ⋃_k B̄_k(0) and H^m(A ∩ B̄_k(0)) < ∞. Hence H^m⌞A′ is σ-finite (in particular s-finite) for every Borel A′ ⊆ A.
6. (Injective Lipschitz pieces.) By CountablyRectifiable m A, A ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_i F_i(Eucl m) with H^m(M₀) = 0 and F_i : Eucl m → E satisfying LipschitzWith K_i F_i.
   - Fix i and let R_i := areaRegularSet F_i, which is Borel by (L2). For b ∈ R_i, F_i has Fréchet derivative fderiv ℝ F_i b at b, hence HasFDerivWithinAt F_i (fderiv ℝ F_i b) R_i b.

   - Apply (L4) to F_i, s := R_i, f′ := fderiv ℝ F_i and r. This gives pairwise disjoint Borel sets t_{i,l} (l ∈ ℕ) with R_i ⊆ ⋃_l t_{i,l}, and continuous linear maps A_{i,l}, with the following properties.
     - Put S_{i,l} := R_i ∩ t_{i,l} (Borel). Then ‖F_i(b) − F_i(b′) − A_{i,l}(b − b′)‖ ≤ r(A_{i,l})·‖b − b′‖ for b, b′ ∈ S_{i,l}.
